351	    [IsLocallyNoetherian C.left] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne C.left]
352	    [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
353	    (P : C.left.PrimeDivisor) :
354	    HasRationalResidues k P := by
355	  intro f hf
356	  rcases eq_or_ne f 0 with rfl | hf0
357	  · refine ⟨0, ?_⟩
358	    rw [map_zero, sub_zero]
359	    exact (orderGe P 1).zero_mem

362	    ((mem_orderGe_of_ne_zero hf0).mp hf)

365	    isClosed_primeDivisor (coheight_le_one_of_curve C) P

377	as "the gated keystone input, not re-proved here".  It is now **provable** on curve

379	finiteness at all: approximation by constants says every class in the quotient is a

383	`residueDeg_eq_one_iff_hasRationalResidues` would require the finiteness binder, since that

389	If every function regular at `P` agrees with a constant to first order, then
390	`κ(P) = orderGe P 0 ⧸ orderGe P 1` is spanned by the class of `1`, hence finitely generated.

392	Stated on `HasRationalResidues` rather than on curve hypotheses so that it is reusable: this
393	is the general fact that the approximation statement is *strictly stronger* than the
394	finiteness gate N14 assumes.  The spanning computation is the one in the `←` branch of

397	theorem finite_localStepTgt_one_of_hasRationalResidues
398	    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
399	    [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X] [Algebra k X.functionField]
400	    [IsConstantField k X] (P : X.PrimeDivisor)
401	    (happrox : HasRationalResidues k P) :
402	    Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1) := by
403	  have hone : (1 : X.functionField) ∈ orderGeSub k P (1 - 1) := by
404	    rw [mem_orderGeSub]
405	    exact Or.inr (by rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_one]; norm_num)
406	  -- every class is a `k`-multiple of the class of `1`
407	  have hspan : (⊤ : Submodule k (localStepTgt k P 1)) ≤
408	      Submodule.span k {Submodule.Quotient.mk (p := Submodule.comap
409	        (orderGeSub k P (1 - 1)).subtype (orderGeSub k P 1)) ⟨1, hone⟩} := by
410	    intro z _
411	    obtain ⟨g, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ z
412	    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := happrox (g : X.functionField)
413	      (by
414	        have hg2 := g.2
415	        rw [mem_orderGeSub] at hg2
416	        exact orderGe_antitone (by norm_num) hg2)
417	    rw [Submodule.mem_span_singleton]
418	    refine ⟨c, ?_⟩
419	    rw [← Submodule.Quotient.mk_smul, Submodule.Quotient.eq, Submodule.mem_comap,
420	      Submodule.subtype_apply]
421	    have hval : ((c • ⟨1, hone⟩ - g : orderGeSub k P (1 - 1)) :

423	      change c • (1 : X.functionField) - (g : X.functionField) = _
424	      rw [Algebra.smul_def, mul_one]
425	      ring
426	    rw [mem_orderGeSub, hval]

428	  -- a module whose `⊤` sits inside a one-vector span is finitely generated
429	  have htop : (⊤ : Submodule k (localStepTgt k P 1))
430	      = Submodule.span k {Submodule.Quotient.mk (p := Submodule.comap
431	        (orderGeSub k P (1 - 1)).subtype (orderGeSub k P 1)) ⟨1, hone⟩} :=

\chapter{Adelic Riemann--Roch: the repartition cokernel (RR.A)}
\label{chap:RiemannRoch_Adelic}

\section{The two-chart model}
\label{sec:RiemannRoch_Adelic_intro}

Let \(C\) be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field
\(k\), and let \(K=k(C)\).  The divisor theory of
\Cref{chap:RiemannRoch_WeilDivisor} assigns to every prime divisor \(P\)
an order \(v_P\colon K^\times\to\mathbb Z\).  The Mayer--Vietoris theory
of \Cref{chap:Cohomology_MayerVietoris} computes the first cohomology of
the structure sheaf from two affine charts.

\paragraph{The concrete-repartition idea.}
Classically (Weil), for the function field \(K = k(C)\) one forms the
\emph{adele} (repartition) space
\(\mathbb{A}_K = \{(x_P)_P \in \prod_P K : v_P(x_P) \ge 0 \text{ for
almost all } P\}\), its bounded subspaces
\(\mathbb{A}_K(D) = \{(x_P) : v_P(x_P) \ge -D(P)\ \forall P\}\), and the
two Riemann--Roch spaces
\[
  L(D) = K \cap \mathbb{A}_K(D)
        = \{ f \in K : \operatorname{div} f + D \ge 0\},
  \qquad
  H^1(D) = \mathbb{A}_K / (\mathbb{A}_K(D) + K).
\]
The genus is \(g=\dim_k H^1(0)\), and the index of speciality is
\(i(D)=\dim_k H^1(D)\).  A two-affine cover gives a finite presentation
of the same cohomology without first constructing the restricted product.

\paragraph{The \(2\)-affine-cover cokernel.}
Fix affine opens \(U_0,U_1\) covering \(C\), with affine intersection, and
write
\[
  A_i = \Gamma(U_i, \struct{C}), \qquad
  A_{01} = \Gamma(U_0 \cap U_1, \struct{C}).
\]
The degree-\(1\) Čech cohomology of the two-element cover is the cokernel
of the difference map \((f_0, f_1) \mapsto f_0|_{01} - f_1|_{01}\):
\[
  \check{H}^1 \;=\; A_{01} \big/ (A_0 + A_1).
\]
For a Weil divisor \(D\) the \emph{twisted} version replaces each ring of
sections by the Riemann--Roch sheaf of sections
\(\Gamma(U, \struct{C}(D)) = \{ f \in K : v_P(f) \ge -D(P) \text{ for all
prime divisors } P \in U\}\), giving
\[
  L(D) = \Gamma(U_0, \struct{C}(D)) \cap \Gamma(U_1, \struct{C}(D)).
\]
\[
  \check{H}^1(D) = \Gamma(U_0 \cap U_1, \struct{C}(D)) \big/
    \bigl(\Gamma(U_0, \struct{C}(D)) + \Gamma(U_1, \struct{C}(D))\bigr).
\]
The bridge of \Cref{sec:RiemannRoch_Adelic_cokernel} identifies
\(\check H^1(0)\) with \(H^1(C,\struct C)\).

\]

\chapter{Adelic Riemann--Roch: the repartition cokernel (RR.A)}
\label{chap:RiemannRoch_Adelic}

\section{The two-chart model}
\label{sec:RiemannRoch_Adelic_intro}

Let \(C\) be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field
\(k\), and let \(K=k(C)\).  The divisor theory of
\Cref{chap:RiemannRoch_WeilDivisor} assigns to every prime divisor \(P\)
an order \(v_P\colon K^\times\to\mathbb Z\).  The Mayer--Vietoris theory
of \Cref{chap:Cohomology_MayerVietoris} computes the first cohomology of
the structure sheaf from two affine charts.

\paragraph{The concrete-repartition idea.}
Classically (Weil), for the function field \(K = k(C)\) one forms the
\emph{adele} (repartition) space
\(\mathbb{A}_K = \{(x_P)_P \in \prod_P K : v_P(x_P) \ge 0 \text{ for
almost all } P\}\), its bounded subspaces
\(\mathbb{A}_K(D) = \{(x_P) : v_P(x_P) \ge -D(P)\ \forall P\}\), and the
two Riemann--Roch spaces
\[
  L(D) = K \cap \mathbb{A}_K(D)
        = \{ f \in K : \operatorname{div} f + D \ge 0\},
  \qquad
  H^1(D) = \mathbb{A}_K / (\mathbb{A}_K(D) + K).
\]
The genus is \(g=\dim_k H^1(0)\), and the index of speciality is
\(i(D)=\dim_k H^1(D)\).  A two-affine cover gives a finite presentation
of the same cohomology without first constructing the restricted product.

\paragraph{The \(2\)-affine-cover cokernel.}
Fix affine opens \(U_0,U_1\) covering \(C\), with affine intersection, and
write
\[
  A_i = \Gamma(U_i, \struct{C}), \qquad
  A_{01} = \Gamma(U_0 \cap U_1, \struct{C}).
\]
The degree-\(1\) Čech cohomology of the two-element cover is the cokernel
of the difference map \((f_0, f_1) \mapsto f_0|_{01} - f_1|_{01}\):
\[
  \check{H}^1 \;=\; A_{01} \big/ (A_0 + A_1).
\]
For a Weil divisor \(D\) the \emph{twisted} version replaces each ring of
sections by the Riemann--Roch sheaf of sections
\(\Gamma(U, \struct{C}(D)) = \{ f \in K : v_P(f) \ge -D(P) \text{ for all
prime divisors } P \in U\}\), giving
\[
  L(D) = \Gamma(U_0, \struct{C}(D)) \cap \Gamma(U_1, \struct{C}(D)).
\]
\[
  \check{H}^1(D) = \Gamma(U_0 \cap U_1, \struct{C}(D)) \big/
    \bigl(\Gamma(U_0, \struct{C}(D)) + \Gamma(U_1, \struct{C}(D))\bigr).
\]
The bridge of \Cref{sec:RiemannRoch_Adelic_cokernel} identifies
\(\check H^1(0)\) with \(H^1(C,\struct C)\).

Because \(k\) need not be algebraically closed, every place carries a

  \deg P \;=\; [\kappa(P) : k] \;=\; \dim_k \kappa(P) \;<\; \infty,
  \qquad
  \deg_k D \;=\; \sum_P D(P)\,\deg P .
\]
